title: If You Had a Million Tenge…
paragraphs: A journalism student at WKU recently asked five classmates a simple hypothetical question: "If you had a million tenge right now — not a loan, not an investment, just a gift — what would you do with it?" The answers were revealing. Not because of what the students would spend the money on, but because of what their answers said about their values, their fears, and the kind of future they were trying to build.

Kamila's response was immediate. "I'd use half of it to fund a year of studying abroad — somewhere in Europe, ideally Scotland, because of the linguistics programmes. If I had the money, I wouldn't hesitate. The other half I'd put in savings. I know that's boring," she added, "but if I had a financial cushion, I'd feel much less anxious about my future. Security is underrated."

Amir thought for longer. "If I had a million tenge, I'd invest about 600,000 in technology stocks — specifically, emerging market ETFs. That's around 1,200 euros, which is a reasonable starting position. I wouldn't touch the rest for a year. Then I'd see. Maybe I'd start a small software product if the investments grew."

Rustam didn't hesitate either, but for different reasons. "I'd travel," he said simply. "If I had that kind of money, I'd go to Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Turkey — overland, by train and bus. It would cost maybe 300,000 tenge for three months. The rest I'd keep for emergencies." He paused. "Actually — I'd also buy a decent pair of boots. Mine are falling apart."

Zhibek was the most strategic. "If I had a million tenge, I wouldn't spend it straight away. I'd sit on it for a month and think. Then I'd probably split it between a coaching course for volleyball training methodology — if I were going to do this long-term, I'd want to be certified — and a laptop upgrade. My current one is three years old and struggling."

Daniyar was the most surprising. "I'd give 200,000 to my parents," he said. "My father's business has been difficult this year. If I had extra money, I wouldn't keep it all for myself. After that, I'd invest the rest in the family business — maybe open a second branch. If it worked, we'd employ two or three more people from our town."

The journalism student asked one follow-up question: "If you didn't have any financial worries at all — if money were no object — what would you do differently with your degree?" The answers were unanimous: they would all choose exactly the same courses. "That tells you something," she wrote in her notes. "They don't study what they study for money. They study it because they love it."

A million tenge is about 2,000 euros at the current exchange rate. It is not a fortune. But it is enough to reveal a great deal about a person — what they value most, what they are afraid of, and what they would do if the world gave them a small, unexpected chance.

dialogue.text: If you had the money, would you actually go to Scotland, Kamila?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Without a doubt. If I had the funding, I'd apply tomorrow. The linguistics programme there is incredible.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: I wouldn't go to Scotland. If I had the money, I'd explore Central Asia first.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I'd invest it. If you put money in the right places early, it grows.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: You're all so different. I wouldn't do any of that — I'd wait and think.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's also a choice. What would you do with the time while you waited?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Research my options. If I were going to spend that much, I'd want it to matter long-term.

dialogue.speaker: Daniyar
dialogue.text: I'd give some to my family. If my parents needed it, that would come first.

vocab.definition: based on a possible situation that may not be real
vocab.example: "If you had a million tenge" is a hypothetical question — it's not real.

vocab.definition: giving you surprising new information about someone
vocab.example: The answers were revealing — they showed what students truly value.

vocab.definition: agreed by everyone in a group
vocab.example: The answers were unanimous — all five would choose the same courses.

vocab.definition: done as part of a plan to achieve a long-term goal
vocab.example: Zhibek was the most strategic — she wouldn't spend without thinking first.

vocab.definition: to pause before doing something because you are uncertain
vocab.example: "If I had the money, I wouldn't hesitate." — no pause, immediate action.

vocab.definition: officially recognized as having the required skills
vocab.example: "If I were going to do this long-term, I'd want to be certified."

vocab.definition: to put money into something to gain profit or benefit later
vocab.example: "If I had a million tenge, I'd invest 600,000 in technology stocks."

vocab.definition: to come into being or become known
vocab.example: "Emerging markets" = markets growing and becoming more significant.
